replacements.before:
**SIMD Resonator** is a dedicated 128-mode playable body. A tap or drag places and hardens the strike while material presets move between glass, wood, bent metal, and pinned wire without changing the instrument's established modal DSP. Four-lane `f32x4` runs automatically where available and preserves scalar Wasm as its silent fallback.

**[Rust Resonator](simd-resonator-rust.html)** keeps the original SIMD Resonator beside a Rust WebAssembly copy with up to 4,096 independently ringing modes. It opens at 512 modes across a 128-order spectral span; Modes controls density while Spectral span controls the frequency range. Twenty complete presets include twelve classic body/FFT states and eight dense modal demonstrations. The modal core uses four-lane `f32x4` with a Rust scalar fallback; the existing JavaScript FFT input path retains its 128-band ceiling. Microphone, local file, and looping sample input remain separate from presets and Audio arming. [Controls, bounds, and implementation](docs/simd-resonator-rust.md).

**SIMD SYNTH** turns the WebGPU Shader Synth and Modular Shader Synth vocabulary into one immediately playable semi-modular rack. Eight polyphonic voices run as two `f32x4` Wasm packs through two interchangeable generators, six combine modes, a reorderable shaper and dual-filter path, six filter topologies, two reorderable time-effect slots, and four per-voice/global modulation routes. The fixed patch-wide topology avoids a cable canvas while still letting presets recombine vector, FM, wavefold, modal, particle, additive, formant, and bytebeat sources. A real-output scope, press-to-play X/Y surface, chromatic keyboard, browser MIDI, 16-step pitch/gate/accent/slide sequencer, one-tap Init/Undo/Panic, and browser-local preset recall keep experiments recoverable. SIMD loads automatically with an explicit scalar Wasm fallback; Audio arming remains independent from transport.
